claims.text: AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 can be produced as a dense bulk HEA by powder-metallurgical processing.
The AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 material contains two finely distributed body-centered-cubic phases.
A secondary phase with a complex crystal structure can precipitate during spark-plasma sintering of AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5.
Controlled thermal oxidation of AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 will produce a uniform and adherent spinel oxide layer.
The thermally formed spinel layer will significantly improve tribo-corrosion resistance at elevated temperature.
Optimizing oxidation temperature and time will promote a self-renewing protective spinel layer.
AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 exhibits improved wear resistance under elevated-temperature reciprocating wear because a protective oxide layer forms in atmospheric conditions.
The proposed protection applies during exposure to reactive gases or salt-containing corrosive environments.
The engineered surface layer is a dense spinel formed from alloy constituents such as Al, Cr, and Ti.
The engineered oxide serves as a diffusion barrier and passivation layer.
Controlled oxidation accelerates formation of a compact, self-healing oxide film.
A protective oxide film mitigates elevated-temperature wear by limiting direct exposure of the underlying metal.
The oxide film mitigates the synergistic effects of tribological stress and corrosion.
Thermally oxidized samples will have lower wear rates than untreated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 samples.
Thermally oxidized samples will exhibit less oxidation-related mass loss than untreated samples.
Improved wear and oxidation resistance will extend component service life.
Untreated AlCoCrFeNiTi0.5 forms an oxide layer during elevated-temperature wear.
The oxide formed on untreated material is non-optimized and offers only moderate protection.
Improper oxidation temperature or duration can produce a non-uniform or excessively brittle oxide layer with inadequate protection.
